title: Finite-free stage of the strict internal-Hom roof
statement: Use the models and roof of [def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-models, def-sfb-internal-hom-strict-roof]. Let R be a ring sheaf and T an R-module sheaf isomorphic to a finite power R^d, with d a nonnegative integer. For every two unbounded cochain complexes P,L, both the normalized comparison a_T:T tensor Hom(P,I_R(L)) -> Hom(P,I_R(T tensor I_R(L))) and the denominator v_T=homFixed(P)(T tensor eta_L) are quasi-isomorphisms. No continuity or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14 (continuity and coefficient passage), Remark 6.8.15 (ambient operations); conditional ring-sheaf comparison is an agent formulation of the argument extracted from returned step 8, not a verbatim assertion of the source.

proof.text: Choose an isomorphism T=R^d. Tensor by T is a finite sum of the identity, hence exact; it preserves the augmentation quasi-isomorphism. Functorial K-injective replacement and Hom into K-injectives preserve this quasi-isomorphism, proving the denominator assertion.

The sectionwise tensor-unit isomorphism sends x to 1 tensor x. The single-complex total-tensor isomorphism gives the same formula for complexes. Evaluating the normalization of the comparison on these sections identifies the rank-one comparison, after this tensor-unit isomorphism, with Hom(P,-) applied to the composite of the inverse tensor-unit isomorphism and the target K-injective augmentation. This is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives, so Hom preserves it.

Tensor with a fixed complex and the raw Hom(P,-) functor are additive, hence preserve finite products. Applying the first to a finite-power presentation of T shows that T tensor I_R(L) is a finite product of K-injectives and therefore K-injective. The natural transformation from raw Hom(P,T tensor I_R(L)) to its resolved representative is a quasi-isomorphism at T and at the unit. After taking homology it transports the finite-product limit cone of the raw Hom functor to the resolved Hom functor. Naturality of the comparison and the rank-one calculation then show that the comparison at T is an isomorphism on every homology object. Empty products cover rank zero without any additional assumption.

lean.statement:
theorem internalHom_finiteFree_stage (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v r})
    (T : Modules.{u, v, r} J R)
    (hfree : ∃ d : ℕ, Nonempty
      (T ≅ limit (Discrete.functor (fun _ : Fin d ↦
        SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v r} RingCat.{max u v r})).obj R)))))
    (P L : CochainComplex (Modules.{u, v, r} J R) ℤ) :
    QuasiIso ((comparison.{u, v, r} J R P L).app T) ∧
      QuasiIso (roofDenominator.{u, v, r} J R P L T)
